title: Frequency Edits on Overlapping Sensor Supply in Plan Member Waiver Counts, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
# Payer frequency edits on overlapping CGM sensor supply

Benefits Verification Bulletin, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

A payer's frequency edit decides which 30-day blocks of a new delivery of the CGM supply allowance (A4239) the payer is expected not to pay because they overlap supply the payer already paid for. This bulletin states how those blocks are marked at risk when Larkfield counts the units a plan member waiver covers for the next delivery on a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment.

## Terms

- The latest refill's claim is the latest claim submission billing the latest refill shipment of the CGM supply allowance on the program.
- A remittance for that claim is a claim remittance answering it; the payer paid any amount on the claim when the payer paid amounts on its remittances total more than zero, whether that is part or all of the claim.
- The delivery ships today and is divided into 30-day blocks: the first block begins today, the second 30 days after today, the third 60 days after today, and so on for as many blocks as the delivery carries.

## The rule

The frequency-edit adjustment replaces which blocks of the delivery are at risk against the paid-supply end, by these rules:

1. When the payer paid any amount on the latest refill's claim, every 30-day block that begins before the paid-supply end is at risk.
2. When a remittance for that claim posted with no payer payment, only the delivery's first block is at risk, and only when the paid-supply end is after today.
3. Otherwise (no remittance for that claim is on record) the standard at-risk blocks apply: every 30-day block of the delivery is at risk when the paid-supply end is after today, and none when it is not.

## Decision table

| Remittance record for the latest refill's claim | Paid-supply end later than today | Paid-supply end today or earlier |
|---|---|---|
| payer paid more than zero | each block beginning before the end date | none (no block begins before it) |
| remittance posted, payer paid nothing | the first block only | none |
| no remittance posted | every block (the standard at-risk blocks) | none |

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

Take a hypothetical delivery of three 30-day blocks, beginning today, 30 days after today and 60 days after today.

- Paid-supply end 40 days after today, payer paid any amount on the claim: the blocks beginning today and 30 days after today begin before the end date; 2 blocks are at risk.
- Paid-supply end exactly 30 days after today, payer paid the whole claim: the second block begins on the end date, not before it; 1 block is at risk.
- Paid-supply end 40 days after today, remittance posted with no payer payment: 1 block is at risk.
- Paid-supply end 40 days after today, no remittance posted: all 3 blocks are at risk.
- Paid-supply end yesterday: no block is at risk under any of the three rules.
